plan.experiment: orbit-accuracy-experiments, sdn-gp-starlink-ffm-match, amendment A11, M29 (real reentries)

samples.A: CORDS observed reentries (16 objects, 380 predictions); truth the observed time
samples.B: objects whose last Space-Track TIP message precedes the archive snapshot (41 objects, 1360 predictions); truth that message's DECAY_EPOCH

plan.predictions: at each element-set epoch in the last 14 days before the reentry, at least 4 h apart: the module's fit on up to 120 h of pseudo-observations of the set history, then reentry; observed daily space weather
plan.inputs: Space-Track element sets and messages and the CORDS spreadsheet stay in the local archive; the rows below are times, errors and window widths

build.after: wasm sha256 prefix 58c2bef10b55 (the landed sources; the landed wasm differs only by the checkout head it embeds)
build.rescore: all 1,740 predictions re-run on the after build (fit, then reentry on the stored sets); the recorded widths are the module's REENTRY_EPOCH_UNC, and agree with the formula to a relative 4.1e-7
build.one_fit: COSMOS 2572 at 2026-10-19T04:54Z: the fit's B_eff sigma is 0 on the before build and 4.4e-5 on the after build (a 53 km-RMS fit, a variance at zero); the after value is the one scored

model.window: sigma_L^2 = L^2 [ b0^2 + (kappa s)^2 + density_sigma^2 g(L/tau) ], g(x) = (2/x)(1 - (1/x)(1 - exp(-x)))
model.L: time to go from the data cutoff (the fit arc end) to the reentry epoch
model.s: USER_DEFINED_SDNAP_B_EFF_SIGMA / B_eff of the set (the fit's formal sigma)
model.unchanged_options: REENTRY.WINDOW_DENSITY_SIGMA, WINDOW_CORRELATION_DAYS and WINDOW_BALLISTIC_SIGMA keep their meaning and defaults; a WINDOW_BALLISTIC_SIGMA that is set replaces the whole ballistic term

calibration.rule: kappa on the grid 60, 62, ..., 520 that gives the pooled predictions the largest margin min(c1 - 0.60, 0.75 - c1, c2 - 0.90, 0.98 - c2) to the acceptance box, c1 the share within 1 sigma and c2 within 2 sigma of the observed time
calibration.why_this_rule: the pooled coverage cannot reach 68 % and 95 % together on these predictions (the best any window shape reaches at 1 sigma 74 % is 91 % at 2 sigma: 9 Starlinks, 16 % of the objects, make 63 % of the misses at 2 sigma, seven of them changing the fitted B_eff by a factor of 1.6 to 3.1 between the sets far from the reentry and those near it, in both directions (STARLINK-3373 0.013 to 0.039 m^2/kg, STARLINK-1149 0.013 to 0.031, STARLINK-30182 0.063 to 0.029)); the rule takes the point of the frontier with the most room to both bands
calibration.families_tried: a floor in hours, a lead-time exponent on the ballistic term or on the whole window, a long-lead term, a power of s, the fit RMS in place of s, class-aware kappa (oracle): none moves the frontier by more than 0.8 points of margin
calibration.held_out: out of fold: leave one object out (57 folds), 20 repeats of 14 object groups, the two halves split by sorted NORAD within each sample, and 300 random object halves

nine_starlinks.statement: Nine Starlinks cause 63 % of the misses at 2 sigma (101 of 160); they are 16 % of the 57 objects. Seven of them change B_eff by 1.6 to 3.1 times between the sets far from the reentry and those near it, in both directions (STARLINK-3373 and 1149 up, 1828, 30182 and 5693 down); the other two (2382, 30924) keep it near 0.02 m^2/kg and are predicted 33 to 36 % late. This is the known limit of the window and the reason controlled lowering and attitude change need their own treatment.
nine_starlinks.far_near: far: more than 200 h before the observed reentry; near: less than 100 h

limits: The scoring uses observed space weather, so forecast error is not in the window. The predictions run with the daily observed Kp, Ap and F10.7 of their days (the GFZ history), not with a forecast table: the window covers the density model's error and the ballistic coefficient's variability, and a forecast table (F107_DATA_TYPE PRD or PRM days) would add to the density term by an amount this record cannot calibrate.

Nine Starlinks, seven of which change B_eff by 1.6 to 3.1 times between far and near sets, cause 63 % of the 2-sigma misses (nine_starlinks). The Starlinks and the other objects are shown separately: the Starlinks are covered 67.3 % / 88.0 % out of fold, the other objects 96.7 % / 98.7 %.

No set of the 1,740 predictions carries a lowering fit (USER_DEFINED_SDNAP_TAU0 is 0 on all of them): a change of the ballistic coefficient of a Starlink or a controlled disposal is not seen from a 48 to 72 h arc, so the error of those nine objects stays in the tail.

No set feature separates Starlinks from other objects (area under the ROC curve at most 0.63 for B_eff, the formal sigma, the fit RMS, the mean motion, the eccentricity), so the pooled window is as wide for a rocket body as for a Starlink: the other objects are over-covered, 96.7 % within 1 sigma.
The predictions run late by 5 to 7 % at the median (67 % of the Starlink errors are late); the window is symmetric and carries it as spread.
